messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager fired for stream-connector (eu-west-1) — spike in SSE disconnects and tool-call parse errors. error_rate=18% over 5m. link: https://internal.redwood/alerts/1903456789

alex: oncall here, acked. starting triage. Sam, can you grab connector logs and recent deploys for eu-west-1?

sam: got it, pulling logs now. initial look: lots of 502/connection-reset, followed immediately by tool_call parse errors (json decode). suspect truncated frames. sample from stream-worker-4:

```
2026-03-14T22:12:04.128Z stream-worker-4 INFO conn=abc123 client=svc-x SSE disconnected: read ECONNRESET
2026-03-14T22:12:04.130Z stream-worker-4 WARN conn=abc123 tool_call parse_error: unexpected end of JSON input (payload len=512)
2026-03-14T22:12:04.130Z stream-worker-4 DEBUG raw_payload=\"{\"tool\":\"weather\",\"args\":{\"loc\":\"SF\",\"units\":\"c\",...TRUNCATED\"\n```

sam: stack shows retry logic kicking and then a second connect attempt from client. No recent code deploy in eu-west-1 in last 6h.

maria: CS reports 3 enterprise customers in eu-west saw repeated failures in product X starting ~22:11 UTC, spike correlates with alert window. adding severity P1 for customer impact. cs-bot, can you share customer IDs + contact status?

cs-bot: customers impacted: cust-47, cust-211, cust-aws-int. All notified via automated incident message; CS rep on calls with cust-47.

jin: quick mitigation idea: disable tool-call parsing at ingress so we degrade to raw streaming (no tool execution) for eu-west for now. That should stop parse errors and allow clients to continue streaming. Command to flip on edge:

```
# toggle ingress parser for eu-west-1
rdctl config set ingress.eu-west-1.allow_toolcalls=false --reason "mitigate parse errors"
```

alex: good plan. Sam — can you validate that disabling will not break forced-toolcall customers? We need a list of clients using required toolcalls.

sam: running query for clients with enforce_toolcall=true... returning ~12 clients; 3 are enterprise (incl. cust-47). Will coordinate with CS to inform them.

ops-bot: automated check: ingress toggle rolled out to 3 of 4 edge nodes in eu-west-1 (10.0.12x). final node pending, rolling now.

maria: once toggle completes, watch error_rate and customer errors. If successful, we should still keep tracing for raw payloads to capture truncation.

sam: toggle completed at 22:18:11 UTC. immediate drop in parse_error logs from ~18% -> 1.2% in 3m. SSE disconnects still slightly elevated (6%), likely network issues.

alex: good mitigation. next: gather packet-level metrics, tcp retransmits, LB health. Jin — can you check infra (load-balancer backend) for connection resets?

jin: LB logs show occasional TLS/HTTP2 flow resets in same window. suspect intermittent backend insta-restarts on stream-worker-2 (OOM?). checking node metrics.

sam: attaching small timeline snippet for channel (local times are UTC):
- 22:10:05 alert threshold crossed (connectivity + parse errors)
- 22:11:30 CS banner reports first customer error
- 22:12:04 repeated ECONNRESET + parse_error events in logs
- 22:15:00 paging triggered P1
- 22:18:11 ingress parser disabled in eu-west-1 (mitigation)
- 22:19:40 parse_error rate falls to baseline, SSE disconnects drift down over next 10m

maria: hypotheses (ranked):
1) network flapping or LB misconfig causing partial frames -> truncated JSON -> parse errors.
2) client-side change sending malformed chunked frames -> only affects eu-west clients on older SDK.
3) server-side bug in parser that surfaces only under intermittent buffering (edge-case race).

alex: immediate action items:
- sam: collect full raw_payloads for 22:10-22:18 and upload to secure logs bucket (do not redist). tag with request-id.
- jin: check stream-worker-2 process uptime, memory/CPU spikes, and any restarts 22:00-22:20.
- ops-bot: run tcp_retransmit and LB ERR logs query for 22:09-22:20.
- maria/cs-bot: coordinate customer comms and flag enterprise customers for post-mitigation follow-up.

sam: uploaded logs to s3://redwood-incident-logs/1903456789/raw_payloads/ with request-ids. snippet of payloads shows consistent truncation at ~512 bytes only when TLS session renegotiation happens.

jin: stream-worker-2 had a transient OOM-kill at 22:11:58, restarted by k8s. crashloop? investigating container memory limits.

alex: that could align: worker restart causes abrupt connection close -> client submits partial toolcall payload -> parser errors. Good lead.

maria: while we're still in-incident: plan to keep ingress parser disabled for eu-west until we have a fix and node restart pattern stabilizes. create a follow-up RFC for parser resilience and make parser idempotent to partial frames.

sam: added retrospective checklist: fix container memory limit on stream-worker image v3.4.2, add pre-shutdown drain to avoid terminating active SSE sessions, make parser tolerant of truncated frames (log and drop vs raising parse_error).

alex: handing off to maria for next shift — handing off at 00:00 UTC. items to follow-up:
- confirm stream-worker memory limits and redeploy with fix.
- enable ingress parser in eu-west behind a canary flag after verifying stability.
- produce RCA doc with timeline, logs, and post-mortem actions.

maria: taking over. noted tasks and will coordinate with infra to schedule redeploy. leaving incident open until ingress parser re-enabled and metrics normal for 24h.

ops-bot: incident severity set to P1 -> P2 after mitigation. auto-generated timeline attached: https://internal.redwood/incidents/1903456789/timeline

alex: thanks all — great coordination. ping @maria for any escalations overnight.

maria: will do. adding a follow-up: check client SDK versions and roll out a compatibility patch to handle partial payloads in v1.2.1. will include test cases simulating abrupt connection close in our integration suite. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident thread updated. Please file RCA with "stream-worker OOM -> truncated frames -> parse errors" tag when done.
